record.original_question: If a Banach space X is strongly weakly compactly generated, must the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^1(μ, X) also be strongly weakly compactly generated?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2 (Schlüchtermann-Wheeler, [113]). Is the space L^1(μ, X) SWCG whenever X is?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a real Banach space. We say that X is strongly weakly compactly generated (SWCG) if there exists a weakly compact set G ⊂ X such that for every weakly compact set K ⊂ X and every ε > 0 there exists n ∈ ℕ with K ⊂ nG + εB_X, where B_X denotes the closed unit ball of X. Equivalently, the family of all weakly compact subsets of X is strongly generated by a single weakly compact set.

Let (Ω, Σ, μ) be a finite (or σ-finite, non-purely-atomic) positive measure space, and let L^1(μ, X) denote the Lebesgue–Bochner space of (equivalence classes of) Bochner-integrable functions f : Ω → X with norm ‖f‖ = ∫_Ω ‖f(ω)‖ dμ(ω).

Question: If X is SWCG, must L^1(μ, X) also be SWCG?
artifact.category_tag: Banach spaces — SWCG and Lebesgue–Bochner spaces
artifact.status_search_result: The question, originally posed by Schlüchtermann and Wheeler, appears to remain open. Subsequent work (e.g., Rodríguez, 2015–2017) established partial results — for instance, that L^1(μ, X) is SWCG when X is an SWCG subspace of an L^1-space, and reformulations in terms of strong generation of uniformly bounded weakly compact families — but a full answer in general is not reported in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: On the SWCG property in Lebesgue–Bochner spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the open problem of whether L^1(μ,X) is SWCG when X is, providing partial positive results.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is treated as open with partial results obtained.

status_evidence.title: A class of weakly compact sets in Lebesgue-Bochner spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Further work analyzing weak compactness in L^1(μ,X) related to the SWCG property.
status_evidence.claim: Continued investigation of the SWCG transfer problem without full resolution.
